title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Morgan Li
body:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's standards and operational runbooks for the Applied ML evaluation stack: the eval-harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding requirements, quality guardrails, quantization profile management, and regression triage. It is designed for applied ML engineers, SREs supporting model serving, and product partners who own feature-level quality metrics.

Scope and intent:
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist for new models entering the serving fleet.
- Define prompt-set and benchmark hygiene for regression detection and signal quality.
- Standardize quantization profile creation and compatibility tests.
- Document the regression triage playbook: detection, impact analysis, rollback criteria, and postmortem.

Ownership and SLA:
- Primary owner: Applied ML (model-onboarding) squad (engineering).
- Secondary owners: Eng SRE (alerts & capacity), Eng Platform (deploy/rollouts).
- SLOs for eval coverage: new model must have at least 3 prompt-set families covering top-3 customer intents and 1 perf-sensitive benchmark before canary.
- Regression detection SLO: automated eval-run cadence >= once per deploy, with alert within 30 minutes of threshold breach.

High-level components:
1) Eval Harness (CI and on-demand):
   - Purpose: run deterministic batches of prompts against candidate model and baseline(s), produce metrics, diffs, and artifacts (token-level traces, embeddings, log-loss, human-score if available).
   - Outputs: per-prompt metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM as applicable), safety flags, hallucination heuristics, latency & memory profiles, token-cost estimates.
   - Integrations: GitHub PR checks, CI runners, MLflow artifacts bucket, and internal dashboard ingestion (redwood-evals service).

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks:
   - Prompt families: group by intent (e.g., summarization, code-completion, instruction-following). Each family must include: canonical-positive examples (>=50), adversarial negatives (>=10), and edge-cases (>=10).
   - Benchmarks: stable datasets (internal and public) used for longitudinal tracking. Each benchmark has: owner, expected metric ranges, and TTL for refresh.
   - Naming convention: <product>-<intent>-<version> (e.g., console-summarize-v1).

3) Model Onboarding Checklist (must pass before canary deploy):
   1. Model artifact and provenance documented (checkpoint ID, training recipe link, tokenizers, tokenizer version).
   2. Eval harness run against baseline: produce baseline-diff report and artifact link.
   3. Pass quality guardrails: no critical safety flag, acceptable hallucination rate (<=3% on targeted benchmarks), and instruction-following pass rate >= 85% unless owner agrees to exception.
   4. Quantization profile compatibility checks (if quantized variant will be used).
   5. Performance profile: p50/p95 latency on representative sequence lengths under target batch sizes and HW profile.
   6. Cost estimate report and recommended serving configuration (batching, kv-cache policy, quantization).

4) Quality Guardrails (automated + manual):
   - Safety Checker: rule-based and model-based safety signals run in eval harness. Flags are classified as critical/warning/info.
   - Acceptable thresholds: critical safety flags = 0; warning flags <= 1 per 1k prompts.
   - Hallucination heuristic: entity hallucination detector + faithfulness score. Thresholds are benchmark-specific and must be documented in the benchmark metadata.

5) Quantization Profiles and Testing:
   - Profile schema: profile-name, target-precision, calibration-dataset-id, per-layer-ignore-list, expected-accuracy-delta, owner.
   - Recommended profiles:
       * q4_0-default: 4-bit asymmetric, default calibration set, expected accuracy delta <= 2%.
       * q8_0-fast: 8-bit per-tensor, optimized for latency, expected delta <= 0.5%.
   - Validation tests:
       1) Functional parity eval (run eval-harness against float baseline using prompt-sets): accuracy delta must be within expected-accuracy-delta for primary benchmarks.
       2) KV cache correctness test for generation continuity across tokens.
       3) Performance/regression test: measure p95 latency and throughput vs float baseline.
   - Example quant-profile YAML (required fields):

   ---
   profile_name: q4_0-console-instruct
   target_precision: q4_0
   calibration_dataset: console-instruct-calib-v1
   per_layer_ignore: [layer_norm, output_projection]
   expected_accuracy_delta_pct: "<=2.0"
   owner: "applied-ml-models"
   ---

6) Regression triage playbook (detection -> action -> closure):
   - Detection:
     1) Automated eval-run detects metric drift: metric delta > threshold (e.g., instruction-following drop >= 5 percentage points OR hallucination increase >= 3 percentage points) compared to baseline or last-green.
     2) Canary/production monitoring signals (customer error reports, user-level quality alerts) correlate with eval signals.
   - Triage steps (ordered):
     1) Acknowledge and create incident in incident-tracker with tag "model-regression".
     2) Run targeted eval-harness with focused prompt-set (hot-100) and collect artifacts: diff report, token traces, embeddings.
     3) Compare quantized vs float runs to isolate quantization-induced regressions.
     4) Run ablation: zero-shot vs fine-tuned prompts, temperature changes, prompt-length sensitivity.
     5) If user-facing impact is high (see Impact matrix below), trigger rollback to last-green model and open follow-up bug for root cause.
   - Impact matrix (simple):
     * High: customer-facing correctness regressions on top-10 intents OR >5% conversion/engagement drop downstream. -> Immediate rollback.
     * Medium: degraded metric on non-critical benchmarks or internal tooling. -> Patch and staged deploy.
     * Low: minor drift within expected noise bounds. -> Monitor and schedule next retrain/onboarding window.

7) Operational runbook & alert thresholds:
   - Alerts emitted by redwood-evals service:
     * eval.metric.regression (severity=high) -> threshold: delta >= 5 percentage points OR absolute metric < guardrail lower bound.
     * eval.quant.mismatch (severity=medium) -> detected when quantized delta > profile.expected_accuracy_delta.
     * eval.hallucination.spike (severity=high) -> hallucination rate > 3% absolute increase.
   - Notification path: PagerDuty to on-call applied-ml engineer (P1), Slack #applied-ml-alerts, and create GitHub issue with artifacts.

8) Canary and rollout guidance:
   - Canary windows: minimum 48 hours for models with >10k qps-equivalent requests; for low-traffic models, minimum 24 hours and manual review.
   - Canary traffic ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated quality gating at each step. Gate checks: eval-harness scheduled run and production telemetry comparison.

9) Example commands and snippets:
   - Run eval harness (CLI):
     redwood-eval run --model candidate:1234 --baseline model:stable-2026 --prompt-set console-summarize-v1 --output /artifacts/candidate-1234/ --parallel 16

   - Generate quantization profile (CLI):
     redwood-quant profile create --name q4_0-console-instruct --calib-dataset console-instruct-calib-v1 --ignore-layers layer_norm,output_projection --expected-delta 2.0 --owner applied-ml-models

   - Sample eval-harness JSON output (trimmed):
     {"benchmark":"console-summarize-v1","metric":"instruct_pass_rate","baseline":0.92,"candidate":0.89,"delta":-0.03}

10) Postmortem & closure criteria:
   - Postmortem required for any High-impact regression. Must include: timeline, root cause hypotheses, mitigations, action items, and owner assignments.
   - Closure criteria: fixes deployed + verified by targeted eval-harness run and 7-day production telemetry stabilization.

11) Common failure modes and mitigations:
   - False positive from prompt brittleness: add more paraphrases and adversarial negatives to prompt set.
   - Quantization-induced generation artifacts: run per-layer sensitivity analysis and consider per-layer skip or mixed-precision fallback.
   - Data drift in evaluation dataset: rotate calibration and benchmark datasets quarterly and annotate drifted examples.

12) Related artifacts and storage:
   - Artifact store: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{run_id}/ (profiles, diffs, traces).
   - Dashboard: internal redwood-eval-dashboard (links embedded in artifact metadata).

Appendix A \u2014 Example prompt-set table (short):
| prompt_id | intent            | variant        | expected_behavior                       | owner | notes |
|-----------|-------------------|----------------|------------------------------------------|-------|-------|
| PS_CON_01 | summarization     | canonical-1    | concise 2-3 sentence summary             | product-eng | high-priority |
| PS_CON_12 | summarization     | adversarial-1  | contains irrelevant facts to detect halluc. | applied-ml | add paraphrases |

Appendix B \u2014 Quick checklist for PR reviewers (model changes):
- Verify eval-harness green for all required prompt-sets and benchmarks.
- Confirm quantization profile exists and passed validation.
- Ensure artifact links and cost/latency estimates included.
- Check safety flags and confirm mitigations or exceptions documented.
